newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori to thank pope for hostage help.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori to thank pope for hostage help.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori was heading to Rome on Friday to thank Pope John Paul II for his help during Peru's four-month crisis when Marxist rebels held 72 hostages, the government said.

Fujimori will meet on Monday with the pope and Italy's President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro before returning to Peru, which has more than 21 million Roman Catholics, on Tuesday, the government announced in its newspaper El Peruano.

During the hostage siege at the Japanese ambassador's home, the Vatican provided Peruvian Archbishop Luis Cipriani as a mediator to oversee talks between the government and Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels. But his work was ultimately fruitless as Fujimori ordered troops to storm the diplomatic compound on April 22 in a bloody raid that saw one hostage, two commandos, and all 14 hostage-takers die.

The violent end was also potentially embarrassing for the Vatican as the assault was launched with a tip-off via a microphone planted in a crucifix that had been smuggled into the residence, military sources said. Troops also executed at least two captured rebels during the raid, according to the sources and witnesses' testimony.

The pope has first-hand knowledge of the Peruvian guerrillas' work after an epsiode in 1990 when the larger Maoist Shining Path group coordinated an electricity blackout in the whole of Lima to coincide with the religious leader's landing in the capital on a visit.
